questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study in the Netherlands and Amsterdam specifically to take part in the culture and to experience to the life abroad. I also found that the courses at the university were fitting quite well with my program and even gave some opportunities that were not offered at my home university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I throughly enjoyed my studies at VU and the life outside of the study. However my visit was affected by the COVID-19 and limited some of the culture aspects and social activities.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the VU were excellent in giving the information needed by incoming students and also aided by the introduction days at campus.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The information given through mails and at the campus introduction days were extensive and helpful. Beside from that I did not receive any assistance, but I also did not have a need.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university aided me in finding housing, which would otherwise have been quite difficult in Amsterdam. The assistance allowed me to get affordable housing without any issues. I highly recommend looking into the housing provided through the university, since it was comparably cheap and fellow students lives in the buildings, which makes it easier to make friends in your own neighbour hood.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When arriving in the Netherlands you should get a BSN (Citizen service number) as quickly, since if you are over 23 you can apply for rent allowance, which is 297 eur, every month. A BSN also allows you to get a Dutch bank account, which can make payments a lot easier and cheaper.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The first registration is made before the schedule is released which means that schedule clashes might mean you have to alter your choices later on. It was annoying to read up on the courses you were interested in chosing what to register for and then later on to find out the combination of courses were never possible. However besides from that the course information was easy to get and the process was no problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I register for a course were I found out that the prerequisites were not met from my previous studying. So I had to change to course for another. This could have been bad, but the course coordinator in the first selected course helped me and I also was enrolled in a new course without any big issues due to the help from a course coordinator at the new course. This was despite the fact that the deadline was already expired and I really got the help I needed to find the right  course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful, but had to change a course for a new one due to the prerequesites not being met and it being too difficult for that reason. I luckily was able to change without any problems

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not underestimate the requirements of the courses, but even if you do there is always something to be done if you ask for help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the courses interesting and on a generally appropriate academic level

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level aprrioate for most of the courses however the ADMET courses was closer to bachelor level if compared with my studies of pharmacy in my home university. I chose a course of Computer-aided drug design and virtual screening out of interest, but the found the level unsuitable for me, with my background in pharmacy and not really any previous knowledge with the computational modelling. The course was interesting though, but I had to change it due to it being too difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was generally relying on lectures and group work with assignments, with not much classroom teaching besides from the Advanced Molecular Immunology course. The teaching were also online for a lot of the semester due to COVID-19, this might be affected by that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ADMET
Advanced Molecular Immunology
Drug Target Biochemistry and Signalling
Human Cells in Culture
Infectious Diseases and Vaccine Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Advanced Molecular Immunology - gives a in depth knowledge of the immune system and techniques with the field. However the other students generally have a background in the immunology field, so prepare for catching up if you dont. 
Drug Target Biochemistry and Signalling - Interesting course with great teachers. The course has new technologies in the field of drug targets has cool components with give insight in the field of drug target and the life of a researcher. The assignment was to make a research proposal, which was not overwhelming. but made the group work interesting for anyone interested in research. 
Human Cells in Culture - Really usable if want to work with cell culturing and cell methods. The course introduces to techniques, so you dont need to know about cells culturing beforehand since the course covers everything in an approachable way

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have like to partake in social activities at campus to engage more with the Dutch students, but it was not very active due to COVID-19

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was not very active due to COVID-19 and I was at the one Friday bar, but the information on social activities were either not there in english or not at all. I think more activities are held normally when there is not lock down though. Introduction days were a nice start and also made it possible to make new friends with the other exchange students. Most of my friends were made it the introduction days, and we kept contact throughout-

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction days

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: So many museums are available in Amsterdam, I are really cool to experience. Rijkmuseum, Van Gogh, Anne Frank House if you get a museum card (BSN needed) you can visit 600 museums free of charge after the one time purchase. Well worth it in my mind.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think the culture shock was limited because the danish culture are similar in a lot of ways with the dutch. The directness can be wrongly interpreted as being rude, but as a danish person that is perfect. Howevever

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I heard joining the clubs at campus are a good way to meet local students but did not have the upportunity due to lockdown (COVID-19). I personally made a post on reddit to find local people to hang out with through my hobby, which made me make some friends. So social media can be a way to might somebody of the locals who have similar interests as you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think dutch culture is not always so approachable, which makes it a bit harder to make friends. But if you do it is well worth it. In my experience they generally do not go out of their way to invite you in, so you definitely have to make the effort of you want to engange with them. However Vrije has

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The informal way the dutch communicate which makes it easy to say what you mean and limits risk of misunderstandings. Some might consider it rude, but I really like it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
See the city of Amsterdam and do all the touristy stuff while you are there. The exchange is also for you to experience the city. Museum cards make it cheaper on maybe also motivates you to see more than you would otherwise.
Get a bike ASAP while you are there. It is nice to get around plus you get to see much more while you travel. However beware that the dutch, not unlike bikers in Copenhagen drive fast and stops for no one. But if you want to understand the dutch you need to live like the dutch and the bike is a must. 
Chose different courses that have your interests covers. You get the opportunity to chose from a variety of different course that maybe your own program does not include. Use this to expand for academic horizon and also get the perspective of student and lecturers outside for track. Once your education is over you will probably work with people with different academic background anyways and this is a great way see interdisciplinary cooperation and is really useful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You dont need to learn dutch of you are there for one semester only, but it is fun to learn anyways at least to read, since you will be able to pick up a lot quickly if you know English, Danish and German.
Get an BSN (citizen service number) as quick as you can. The process of getting one is kind of slow so start early so you can get a dutch bank account to get a Maestro card many places do not accept Mastercard or Visa, so the Maestro card help a lot in the everyday.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made with the other exchange students, since it was both open my horison to new culture and just a lot of fun. I hope I will be able to maintain the relations and create new experiences with them in the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The lockdown was the biggest challenge, but hopefully that will not be an issue going forward.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
